title: Concurrent chat context corruption and AI quota misclassification
original_report: Inspect the provider and persistent-chat implementation for concrete correctness defects before preparing a stable candidate release.
discovery_scope: Tauri artifact chat orchestration and adaptive context construction
Provider configuration and model discovery paths

candidates.candidate: Concurrent questions can be paired with the wrong answers or omitted from model context
candidates.contract: Only complete question-answer pairs become context, and concurrent conversations must preserve every turn.
candidates.trigger: Persist user1, user2, assistant1, assistant2 before building the next prompt.

candidates.candidate: HTTP 429 responses mentioning an API key are classified as authentication failures
candidates.contract: Authentication and quota failures have distinct localized UI states.
candidates.trigger: Classify AI provider returned 429: API key quota exceeded.

expected: Concurrent completed turns remain correctly paired and HTTP 429 is reported as a quota failure.
actual: The first concurrent question disappeared from context, while the quota error was labeled as authentication.
environment: macOS Apple Silicon, Rust workspace and Vitest frontend, local test environment
reproduction: Two focused Rust unit tests exercise the production context builder and service-error classifier with deterministic inputs.
failure_signal: The context omitted Question one; the classifier returned ai_authentication instead of ai_quota.
root_cause: Chat context retained only one pending user and backend chat calls were not serialized per artifact. Error classification searched for API key before checking the authoritative 429/quota signal.
fix_summary: Added per-artifact backend chat serialization, FIFO recovery for interleaved historical turns, and quota-first error classification.
why_causal: Serialization prevents new interleaving, FIFO preserves already interleaved complete pairs, and prioritizing 429 directly corrects the erroneous branch selection.

fix_files.summary: Serializes each artifact conversation and pairs queued turns FIFO.
Prioritizes quota signals over authentication wording.

checks.name: Focused regressions
checks.detail: Both tests changed from deterministic failure to pass.

checks.name: Rust workspace
checks.detail: cargo test --workspace passed; two pre-existing real-runtime smoke tests remain intentionally ignored.

checks.name: Frontend production build
checks.detail: TypeScript and Vite production build completed.

limitations: The deterministic concurrency regression exercises the production pairing logic; the backend lock is covered by compilation and the broader suite rather than a timed multi-request integration test.
Live provider credentials and a Windows host were not part of this local proof.
residual_risks: Provider fallback attribution and draft-aware model discovery remain untested candidates from the read-only audit.
Stable release readiness still requires native artifact and real-runtime validation on Apple Silicon, Intel macOS, and Windows.
notes: Gate 1 approved only the two focused regression tests.
Gate 2 approved the four production files and the exact causal transformation.
No dependencies or public command signatures changed.
